rationale: Check round: all four round-1 findings are resolved by current source (see finding_status), confirmed independently against this session's own live-Postgres probes, not only against the carried-forward checker notes. CR-005 is a new finding raised as an inline review comment after round 1 (sibling fallback windows tied on start but not on end double-counted an overlapping request) and is fixed in this round: parent_usage now divides each request by request_share, the count of every eligible sibling window its timestamp falls in, not a flat per-group ties count; the same split is baked into _model_sums so dispatch_money needs no further division. The regression test now asserts conservation (the siblings' shares sum to exactly the eligible requests, not more). The CLI-side criteria (A1, A2, resolver, CLI docs) remain outside this API diff; their presence was confirmed in the sibling CLI repo but not reviewed here, so confidence stays medium on those items alone. 0 deferred; no backlog file written.

Waived, not patched: the launched CTE is unchanged by design. Verified live in this round (a TOOL span with a TOOL_EXECUTION span, a SubagentStart/Stop pair and real LLM usage but no agent.tool.start/.end/.error): call_ids resolves no row for that tool_use_id (its first_ts filter requires an AGENT_CALL_TOOLS-tagged row), so the review's suggested 'UNION SELECT tool_use_id FROM call_ids WHERE agent_id IS NOT NULL' patch is a no-op against the exact scenario it targets - the dispatch row is empty either way. reader.py's launched comment and cli-analytics-events.md already state the rule's second, intentional resolution: a stop alone names no call, in every form. No code change; disposition only.
fallback_start.start_ts uses begin_ts (SubagentStart or call start, no agent_end fallback) for in-scope calls, falling back to t.span_start when both are missing; never starts at the call's own end.
B5 totals assertions at test_live_foreground_agent_run.py lines ~253-271, asserting session totals equal the sum of every stored request. Run live in this round.

New in this round (inline comment, not a round-1 finding): sibling fallback windows tied on start but not on end each took a full, undivided share of an overlapping request (test_siblings_tied_on_start_but_not_on_end_each_take_their_own_window totalled $4 from $3 of eligible requests). Fixed by request_share: each request is divided by the count of every eligible sibling window its timestamp falls in, baked into both the SQL sums and _model_sums' per-model weight; dispatch_money no longer divides separately. The now-redundant ties column was removed. Regression test rewritten to assert conservation; verified live (41/41 tests in test_live_foreground_agent_attribution.py, full non-live CLI Analytics suite, ruff).
